collection_summary:
Original `multi_hop` instance filling one of the remaining gap-4 categories (multi_hop: 0 reg + 1 staged → 2 staged after this instance). NEW **Science/Space Exploration** subdomain — Science family extends from 6 (Academia ×2, Astronomy, History of Science, Mathematics, Physics) to 7 with Space Exploration. Entity: Apollo missions × crew astronauts (NEW entity class — neither countries nor cities/continents). Natural human query: 'For each Apollo mission that landed astronauts on the Moon, list the three crew members with their roles, the year, and each astronaut's birth year.'

Multi-wiki source plan (7 URLs): Wikipedia 'List of Apollo astronauts' as the master article (universe + crew + birth years tabulated together) + 6 per-mission Wikipedia articles (Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17) for cross-validation of crew assignments. Multi-hop chain: Apollo missions → mission crew assignments → astronaut biographical attributes. Result: 18 rows × 5 columns (Mission, Astronaut, Role, Year of Mission, Astronaut Birth Year), composite PK (Mission, Astronaut), 0 duplicates.

Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) composite PK explicit (Mission, Astronaut) — single unambiguous entity-pair; (b) per-row Wikipedia citation via two source families (per-mission articles supply crew + year, master astronauts article supplies birth years); (c) explicit relation commitment in title and db_analog (universe = 6 successful lunar landings; Role = mission crew role; Year = calendar year of lunar surface activity); (d) deterministic universe filter (excludes Apollo 13 abort, excludes Apollo 8/10 orbital-only); (e) stable historical record — no temporal-sensitivity risk.

Cycle-1 audit fix: a linter blanked the cycle-0 curation.json content (all fields empty); cycle-1 fully reconstructed all curation fields with the staged content plus addresses the audit's BLOCKING (blank skeleton) and 1 HYG (temporal_note 'spanned year-boundaries' wording — none of the 6 Apollo lunar-landing missions actually spanned a year boundary).
source_coverage_notes:
Seven Wikipedia source URLs combine to support the multi-hop chain.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Apollo_astronauts): universe + value (Astronaut Birth Year column for all 18 rows). The article's biographical tabulation lists every Apollo astronaut with birth date, mission assignments, and role. Used as the master source for birth years and as a cross-validation for crew assignments. Verbatim astronaut tabulation provides the 18 birth-year values used in the staged Astronaut Birth Year column.
- source_urls[1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11): universe + value (Apollo 11 crew assignments + year). Mission article confirms: Commander Neil Armstrong, Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin, Command Module Pilot Michael Collins; launch July 16, 1969; lunar landing July 20, 1969 — Year of Mission = 1969.
- source_urls[2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_12): universe + value (Apollo 12 crew + year). Confirms Conrad / Bean / Gordon; launch November 14, 1969; landing November 19, 1969 — Year = 1969.
- source_urls[3] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_14): universe + value (Apollo 14 crew + year). Confirms Shepard / Mitchell / Roosa; mission January 31 - February 9, 1971; lunar landing February 5, 1971 — Year = 1971. (No year-boundary crossing: mission start through finish all in 1971.)
- source_urls[4] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_15): universe + value (Apollo 15 crew + year). Confirms Scott / Irwin / Worden; mission July 26 - August 7, 1971; lunar landing July 30, 1971 — Year = 1971. (No year-boundary crossing.)
- source_urls[5] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_16): universe + value (Apollo 16 crew + year). Confirms Young / Duke / Mattingly; landing April 21, 1972 — Year = 1972.
- source_urls[6] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_17): universe + value (Apollo 17 crew + year). Confirms Cernan / Schmitt / Evans; mission December 7-19, 1972; landing December 11, 1972 — Year = 1972 (final Apollo lunar landing; Schmitt is the only professional scientist — geologist — to walk on the Moon). (No year-boundary crossing.)

Validation note: every (Mission, Astronaut) pair is verifiable in both the per-mission article (which lists the crew) and the master List-of-Apollo-astronauts article (which lists each astronaut's mission assignments). Birth years are verifiable in the master article's astronaut tabulation. Crew-role labels (Commander / Lunar Module Pilot / Command Module Pilot) are standardized roles used consistently across all per-mission articles.

Universe-size sanity: 6 missions × 3 crew = 18 rows; 18 unique astronauts (no astronaut flew on more than one Apollo lunar-landing mission). The 6-mission universe is the complete set of successful Apollo lunar landings — Apollo 13 (abort), Apollo 8 (lunar orbit only), Apollo 10 (lunar orbit dress-rehearsal), and earlier Apollo missions (1, 4-9 included) are excluded per the source-defined 'successful lunar landing' filter. Astronaut John Young also flew on Apollo 10 (orbital) and command-module-piloted Gemini missions; this instance only counts his Apollo 16 commander role.
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with three documented risks. R1: 'landed astronauts on the Moon' interpretation — strict reading (only CMDR + LMP who set foot, 12 moonwalkers) vs inclusive reading (all 3 mission crew, mission landed). Committed to inclusive reading with Role column distinguishing landers (CMDR+LMP) from orbital (CMP). The natural query says 'mission that landed astronauts' — the mission landed (= successful surface mission), so all 3 crew members are part of that mission. R2: year choice — committed to Year = calendar year of lunar surface activity. None of the 6 lunar-landing missions actually crossed a year boundary in their mission duration (cycle-1 audit hygiene fix: cycle-0 temporal_note incorrectly said Apollo 14/15/17 'spanned year-boundaries' — none did; Apollo 14 was Jan 31 - Feb 9, 1971; Apollo 15 was July 26 - Aug 7, 1971; Apollo 17 was Dec 7-19, 1972). R3: 'mission landed' filter — Apollo 13 spacecraft did not land (oxygen-tank abort en route); Apollo 8/10 were orbital-only. Filter is unambiguous.
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed addresses Apollo missions directly; closest seeds in shape are #15 (planets × named moons — entity-partition × items) and #19 (scientific disciplines × top 5 scientists — partition × items). The Apollo shape is multi-hop (mission → astronaut → birth-year) which is structurally distinct from both seeds.
- Category: multi_hop — primary because the load-bearing primitive is a chained join (Mission → CrewAssignment → AstronautAttributes) over 3 entity sets. Secondary: implicit_join — single shared key (astronaut name) across two of the three entity sets.
- Source plan: 7 Wikipedia URLs (1 master List-of-Apollo-astronauts + 6 per-mission articles).
- Expected shape: 18 rows × 5 cols, composite PK (Mission, Astronaut).
- Domain: Science/Space Exploration — NEW subdomain per domain_taxonomy.md (Science family was previously at 6 subdomains: Academia ×2, Astronomy, History of Science, Mathematics, Physics; Space Exploration extends to 7).
- Risks/adaptation: per the three pre-gate risks above. Additional minor risks: (a) the staged universe is 18 rows; clears the 10-row floor comfortably; (b) only 12 of 18 astronauts actually walked on the Moon — the Role column makes this distinction explicit; (c) Apollo 13 exclusion is a natural-query interpretation point — an LLM under test that includes Apollo 13's would-be crew (Lovell/Swigert/Haise) would be incorrect under the staged 'successful landing' rule.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Universe filter = 'successful lunar landing' (mission's spacecraft landed astronauts on the Moon): 6 missions — Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17. Excluded: Apollo 13 (abort), Apollo 8/10 (orbital-only), Apollo 1/4-9 (no lunar attempt; Apollo 1 fatal fire pre-launch).
2) Crew inclusion: all 3 mission crew members per mission (Commander, Lunar Module Pilot, Command Module Pilot). Total = 18 astronauts; 12 walked on the Moon (CMDR + LMP), 6 stayed in lunar orbit (CMP). The Role column captures the distinction. An alternative would be to restrict to the 12 moonwalkers, dropping the CMPs; this would yield 12 rows (still clears floor). Chose inclusive interpretation because (a) the natural query 'mission that landed astronauts on the Moon' refers to the mission, not just the lander-bound crew; (b) including CMPs preserves the full mission-crew shape; (c) the Role column makes the moonwalker-vs-orbital distinction explicit.
3) Year column = calendar year of lunar surface activity (Year of Mission). All 6 missions' surface activity falls entirely within a single calendar year (no year-boundary crossings). Cycle-1 audit hygiene fix: cycle-0 temporal_note narrative incorrectly described Apollo 14/15/17 as 'spanning year-boundaries' — that wording is wrong; cycle-1 corrected the narrative without changing any year values.
4) Astronaut Birth Year column = year-only (integer) from the master List-of-Apollo-astronauts article's astronaut tabulation. The full birth dates are stable historical record; staged value is the year component only for column-type uniformity (numeric).
5) Role column values: 'Commander', 'Lunar Module Pilot', 'Command Module Pilot' (verbatim from per-mission article infoboxes). Role-order in sort: Cmdr=0, LMP=1, CMP=2 — reflects mission seniority.
6) Astronaut name normalization: uses the form most commonly cited (e.g., 'Buzz Aldrin' not 'Edwin Aldrin'; 'Pete Conrad' not 'Charles Conrad'). Per-mission articles use these common forms in the crew listings.
7) operation_type 'join' chosen — multi-hop's canonical operation_type per artifact-contract.md is 'join' (since multi-hop is a chained-join shape).
8) Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles lessons applied: (a) PK = composite (Mission, Astronaut) — declared upfront in primary_key array; (b) per-row Wikipedia citation via per-mission article + master astronaut article — no relation conflation; (c) explicit relation commitment in title and db_analog (mission-landed = successful spacecraft landing on Moon surface; Role = crew role per mission; Year = calendar year of lunar surface activity; Birth Year = year component of birth date per master article); (d) deterministic universe filter (excludes Apollo 13 abort + Apollo 8/10 orbital-only).
9) Cycle-1 audit fix: linter blanked the cycle-0 curation.json (all 5 required fields empty, no claim_type). Cycle-1 restored full content from cycle-0 plan + audit's narrative-error correction (year-boundary wording).
normalization_decisions: Mission values use Wikipedia article-title forms: 'Apollo 11', 'Apollo 12', 'Apollo 14', 'Apollo 15', 'Apollo 16', 'Apollo 17'. Astronaut values use the common-name form (e.g., 'Buzz Aldrin' not 'Edwin Eugene Aldrin Jr.'; 'Pete Conrad' not 'Charles Conrad'). Role values are verbatim from per-mission article infoboxes: 'Commander', 'Lunar Module Pilot', 'Command Module Pilot'. Year of Mission is integer (calendar year of lunar surface activity). Astronaut Birth Year is integer (year component of full birth date from master List-of-Apollo-astronauts article). Sort order is (Year of Mission ASC, Mission ASC, Role-order ASC where Cmdr=0, LMP=1, CMP=2) — reflects chronological mission order with seniority-ordered crew within each mission.
open_questions: 1) Universe interpretation — 'landed astronauts on the Moon': staged inclusive reading (mission landed → all 3 crew members) vs strict reading (only the 12 moonwalkers). Staged uses inclusive with Role column distinguishing landers from orbital. An LLM under test using strict reading would yield 12 rows (excluding the 6 CMPs); both readings are defensible. 2) Apollo 13 exclusion: the mission's spacecraft did not land (abort). An LLM under test that includes Apollo 13's would-be crew (Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, Fred Haise) would be incorrect under the staged 'successful landing' rule. 3) Astronaut Birth Year is year-only (integer); full birth dates are available but truncated to year for column-type uniformity. 4) Role values use mission-time roles, not later-career roles (e.g., John Young flew Apollo 16 as Commander, but later commanded STS-1 Space Shuttle Columbia; staged Role is his Apollo 16 mission role only). 5) Astronaut common-name form: Buzz Aldrin's legal name was Edwin Eugene Aldrin Jr. until he legally changed it to Buzz Aldrin in 1988; staged uses 'Buzz Aldrin' per current common form. 6) Cross-Apollo participation: some astronauts flew on multiple Apollo missions (John Young: Apollo 10 orbital + Apollo 16 landing; Gene Cernan: Apollo 10 orbital + Apollo 17 landing). Staged only counts their lunar-landing-mission role. 7) The Apollo program included earlier (pre-landing) missions: Apollo 7-10 were crewed but not landings; Apollo 1-6 were unmanned or test (Apollo 1 fatal fire pre-launch). The staged universe is strictly 'successful lunar landing' — Apollo 7-10 are excluded as expected. 8) Apollo program was followed by Apollo-Soyuz Test Project 1975 (joint US-Soviet) which used Apollo command/service module — excluded as not a lunar mission.
